answer: With a Registered domain bound by attestation certificate with a public binding record, the account is only as strong as its binding: the registered domain answers a fresh challenge, the attestation certificate is recorded, and a public binding record keeps one channel from spawning many identities, so losing the channel means losing the identity, and fakes cannot hide behind throwaway channels. The record keeps every nadir visible, so anyone can audit the binding roll. A nectar alone is noise; a wander of verified channels is a pattern the network can trust.
